Royal dinner tonight at 18:00 in the dining room.
Dinner is at six sharp. The King hates waiting.
Menu for tonight's royal dinner, to be served at 18:00.
Everyone will be at the table at six tonight, so the silver must be polished.
The table is already set for dinner. A small card on the King's plate reads "6 o'clock".
Dinner at six again. Father won't wait a single minute for anyone.
An empty vial with a skull label, hidden behind the wine barrels.
One wine bottle has a broken seal that was closed again with fresh wax.
A book about poisons, left open at the page on poisons that cannot be tasted in wine.
A dead mouse lies next to a small puddle of spilled wine.
Someone took the nightshade berries from the stash in the infirmary. Nasty stuff.
A wine glass that smells oddly bitter, as if something was mixed in it.
Someone took a bottle of foxglove from my cabinet this morning.
Someone tore the page about poisons out of the herbal book.
Someone asked me really specific questions about edible poisons today, I told them I didn't know, it was a weird interaction.
Pantry key register: keys held by {list}.
The pantry key? Besides myself, only {list} have one.
Only the chef, the royal family and I may enter the pantry.
I hand out the pantry keys myself. Only {list} have one.
I handed out the pantry key today to {partial_list}.
Seating plan: wine to be poured for {list}.
Juice for the princess. She never drinks wine.
I love a little taste of the wine before it goes to the table.
I've forbidden {excluded} to touch wine. Doctor's orders.
{excluded} sent back their wine at lunch. Said it tasted of vinegar and they won't touch another drop today.
A dropped note without a name: "{murder_place}. Half past six. Come alone, and burn this letter."
Someone asked me if anyone uses {murder_place} around half past six. I told them nobody ever goes there.
Torn draft in the library waste basket: "...{murder_place} at half past six... tell no one..."
A candle and two cups are set out in {murder_place}. A scrap of paper next to them reads "6:30".
I heard someone whisper 'half past six, {murder_place}' behind the library door.
One of my knives is missing from the drawer.
A dagger is hidden in {murder_place}.
One of my daggers is missing from the rack.
An empty dagger sheath lies on the armoury floor.
Someone asked me today whether a small puncture in the aorta would be fatal. Strange question.
As far as I know, only {list} can write.
{excluded} cut their writing hand this morning. They can't hold a pen today.
{list} are the only ones who ever ask me for paper and ink.
The duty roster on the guards room door is signed with a cross by the Head Guard.
Every week someone has to read the orders to me. I never learned my letters.
Someone used my desk to write a letter today. It wasn't {excluded}, they were with me all afternoon.
Library loan book: books borrowed this month by {list}.
I delivered sealed letters today to {partial_list}.
Notice on the armoury door: "Orders for the Weapons master must be read out to him."
Someone's getting secret letters! I saw {partial_list} each reading something in a corner today.
Tea schedule on the kitchen wall: "Evening tea in the parlor, a quarter to seven."
Tea for one, in the parlor, at a quarter to seven. And I am expected to work miracles with a single scone.
The tea table is set for one: a single cup, and a card reading "6:45".
I was asked to have the parlor ready by a quarter to seven.
Note on the parlor door: "Reserved from 6:45. Please do not disturb."
Tea at a quarter to seven in the parlor is a castle tradition. Whoever's turn it is gets an hour of peace.
A saw lies on the floor by the parlor balustrade.
Someone borrowed my best saw this morning and never brought it back.
Someone asked me today how much our old chandeliers weigh. Strange question.
Someone wanted to know how the parlor chandelier is hung. One rope, I told them, tied off up at the balustrade.
Someone borrowed the old book on how this castle was built. The one with the drawings of the chandeliers.
Someone told my men to keep off the parlor balustrade tonight. Said the railing is being repaired.
Today I saw {partial_list} up at the parlor balustrade.
{excluded} burned both hands on a hot pan this morning. They can't grip a thing today.
{excluded} cut their palm on one of my knives this morning. A deep cut. They can't close that hand for the rest of the day.
Only {list} ever take tea in the parlor. The rest of this household has no taste.
Tea order book: tea served in the parlor this week to {partial_list}.
{excluded} never drinks tea. Wine, or nothing at all.
{excluded} despises tea. Called the blend I prepare dishwater. Not that I touch the stuff myself.
Note on the library door: "Quiet reading hour from a quarter past six. Do not disturb."
I was asked to make sure the library is empty by a quarter past six.
Reading in the library at a quarter past six, just as my dinner reaches its climax. Some people have no sense of timing.
A reading lamp is already lit at the corner desk, next to a card reading "6:15".
The library is quietest at a quarter past six. That's when people come to read alone.
The Great Chronicle of the Realm is gone from its shelf. Nobody ever borrows it. It's far too heavy to casually carry around.
This morning someone in the library was weighing books in their hands, one after another. They didn't read a single one.
Someone asked me to fit the Great Chronicle with iron corners. As if it weren't heavy enough already.
Someone borrowed my kitchen scales this morning. They came back covered in old parchment dust. My scales are for flour, not for literature.
Someone came to me this morning with a broken toe. Dropped a book on it, they said. Must have been a monster of a book.
{excluded} has the arms of a sparrow. I've seen them struggle with a bread basket.
{excluded} couldn't swing anything heavier than a quill.
{partial_list} helped carry the heavy chests for the ball this week. Strong backs, all of them.
{excluded} threw out their back this morning. Doctor's orders: nothing heavier than a spoon today.
Library loan book: books borrowed today by {partial_list}.
The Weapons master can't read a word. I read him his orders myself.
Note on the library desk: "Reading desk reserved today by: {partial_list}."
{excluded} broke their reading glasses this morning. They can't read a word until I've ground them a new pair.
{excluded} returned every book they had this morning. Said they're done with reading for a while.
{excluded} asked for supper in their room at a quarter past six tonight.
Note on the throne room door: "Rehearsal for the ball procession, seven o'clock."
There's a rehearsal for the ball in the throne room at seven tonight. I'll make sure the room stays lit.
Seven o'clock rehearsal in the throne room, and I've been told to keep my men out of the room for it.
Dinner waits until after the seven o'clock rehearsal in the throne room. My soufflé will never forgive them.
Seven o'clock in the throne room, a rehearsal for the procession. As if anyone needs practice walking in a line.
Notice: "All who walk in the ball procession: throne room, seven o'clock."
One of my crossbows is missing from the rack, and nobody asked me for it.
Someone took three crossbow bolts from the practice targets this week. Those things are sharp.
Someone asked for a chair by the throne room balustrade. Nobody ever sits up there.
Someone has been shooting at the old targets in the guards wing all morning. I could hear it from the study.
Someone moved the big candelabra away from the throne room balustrade. It's dark up there in the evenings now.
Someone has been asking me how far a crossbow bolt flies before it drops.
{partial_list} were at archery practice this week.
{partial_list} rode out hunting with me this morning.
{excluded} woke up with a nasty eye infection this morning. They can barely see across a room today.
{partial_list} have borrowed crossbows from the guards' store this month.
{partial_list} asked me this morning to have their best clothes pressed for the procession.
{excluded} won't be at the rehearsal tonight. They told me so themselves.
I hear {partial_list} are among those walking in the procession tonight. They'll all want supper after.
{excluded} asked to be left out of the procession tonight.
Note on the infirmary door: "Evening remedies at a quarter past seven. Take your own bottle from the cabinet."
At a quarter past seven everyone comes for their evening remedy. I can't hand them all out, so they take their own bottle from the cabinet.
Supper waits until after a quarter past seven, when half the castle is queuing at the infirmary. Again.
The Doctor asked me to send anyone who feels unwell to the infirmary at a quarter past seven.
At a quarter past seven my men go for their remedies. Bruises and coughs, every evening.
Someone has moved the bottles in my cabinet. Some labels are turned the wrong way round.
Someone asked me what 'aqua' and 'venenum' mean. Water and poison, I told them.
Someone soaked the labels off three of my jam jars this morning. Who does that?
Someone asked me when there's nobody in the infirmary. I told them: never for long.
Someone tore a page out of my book of poisons. The book was back on the shelf, but the page is gone.
One of the Doctor's little bottles is gone from the drying rack. I counted them myself this morning.
Someone asked me today which of my bottles would kill a man the fastest. Said it was for a story.
Someone asked me today who in the castle takes a remedy in the evening. I didn't think much of it, so I showed them the list.
As far as I know, the Weapons master is the only one in the castle who can't read.
Someone read the Doctor's herb book at my desk at midday. It wasn't {excluded}, they were helping me shelve books then.
{excluded} sprained both wrists at sword practice this morning. They can't hold a cup, let alone a little bottle.
{excluded} sat on their reading glasses this morning. They can't read a thing until the Doctor grinds new ones.
Tonight {partial_list} come for their evening remedy.
{excluded} refused my remedy this morning. Said they'd rather be ill than drink my muck.
{partial_list} asked me for honey and hot water this morning. There's a sore throat going around.
{excluded} already took their remedy at noon. They won't need another tonight.
A written coronation speech in the handwriting of {suspect}.
A threatening letter from {victim} to {suspect}.
A note: {suspect} owes {victim} 100 gold coins, to be paid before tomorrow.
{suspect} is madly in love, but their sweetheart only has eyes for {victim}. You should have seen {suspect}'s face this morning.
Order signed by {victim}: "{suspect} is fired tomorrow."
{victim} mocked {suspect} in front of the whole court this morning.
Marriage contract signed by {victim}: {suspect} must marry a foreign noble next month.
Letter from {suspect} to {victim}: "A whole year without pay. This is my last warning."
Order: "{suspect} has failed for the last time. From tomorrow, {victim} takes over all their duties."
Draft of {victim}'s will: "{suspect} receives nothing."
Royal decree signed by {victim}: "All experiments in the infirmary are forbidden. If caught, {suspect} will be banished."
Doctor's lab journal: "Experiment 14. Subject: {suspect}, who was perfectly healthy. Secretly mixed my new potion into their tea. Side effects: hair loss, nightmares. Fascinating!"
Ever since the silver went missing, {victim} hasn't taken their eyes off {suspect}.
Letter signed by {victim}: "{suspect} may never marry a servant. The servant leaves the castle tomorrow."
{victim} threw the book {suspect} spent ten years writing into the fire.
{victim} tells everyone that {suspect} is a thief. Nobody trusts {suspect} anymore.
{victim} saw {suspect} selling the crown's weapons to our enemies across the border.
Letter from {victim} to {suspect}: "Pay me, or the whole court learns how deep in debt you are."
{suspect} said it out loud: the foreign queen will be the ruin of this kingdom.
{victim} keeps warning everyone that {suspect} is a hedge-witch's son who practises witchcraft in the castle.
{victim} spat out {suspect}'s soup in front of the whole court and called it pig slop.
{victim} laughed that {suspect} can't even lift his own sword anymore.
{victim} keeps the household books. She told {suspect} to their face that the numbers don't add up, and that she'll report it tomorrow.
Letter from {victim} to {suspect}: "I know how you really became Master Chef. The old cook didn't fall down those stairs by accident."
{victim} wants a kitchen girl thrown in the dungeon for breaking a cup. {suspect} begged, but {victim} wouldn't listen.
{victim} found out that {suspect} let a stranger into the castle last week, and threatens to tell the King.
{suspect} said the crown should never go to someone as weak as {victim}.
{victim} wants to drive a poor family off the castle lands. {suspect} swore they'd stop it, whatever it takes.
{victim} has been telling the whole court an embarrassing secret about {suspect}. She is furious.
{victim} keeps pushing the King to march on {suspect}'s homeland.
{suspect} is convinced {victim} will use them in his next experiment. They can't sleep anymore.
{suspect} found out that {victim} sells weapons to our enemies. A traitor, he calls him.
{victim} knows {suspect}'s secret, and she can never keep her mouth shut.
Doctor's lab journal: "Experiment 15 requires blood from {victim}. A rare type, and a few drops will not do. It must be obtained soon."
{victim} caught {suspect} reading a forbidden book of dark magic, and wants to tell the King.
{victim} found something in the royal archives about {suspect}'s real parents.
{victim} read {suspect}'s poems aloud at court and claimed they were their own.
{victim} says he is close to proving that {suspect} is plotting against the crown.
{suspect} says {victim} has the King wrapped around her finger, and the whole realm with him.
{suspect} fears that {victim} will strip them of their lands as soon as he is king.
{suspect} says {victim} lets the common people starve while he feasts.
{victim} promised {suspect} a seat on the royal council, then gave it to someone else.
{victim} had {suspect} thrown out of court in front of everyone.
{victim} still laughs at {suspect} for missing the stag at the last royal hunt.
{victim} knows {suspect} forged the King's seal on a royal decree.
{victim} called {suspect} a tasteless fool, in front of the whole kitchen.
{suspect} supports the new reforms, and {victim} has sworn to block them as long as he commands the guard.
{suspect} owes {victim} a fortune for a sword he made, and {victim} wants every coin by tomorrow.
{victim} keeps a record of every book {suspect} borrowed, and some of those books are forbidden.
{suspect} lost a fortune to {victim} at cards this morning, and {victim} wants it paid tonight.
{victim} caught {suspect} with a royal ring in their pocket this morning, and will report it tomorrow.
{suspect} said this morning that {victim} will pay for what happened to their brother.
Letter from {victim} to the King: "{suspect} is having a secret affair. You deserve to know."
{victim} searched {suspect}'s things this morning and found something. {suspect} went white as a sheet.
{victim} refused to treat {suspect}'s sick sister in the village this morning. She's only getting worse.
{victim} told the King this morning that {suspect} is unfit to rule. And the King listened.
The whole hallway heard {suspect} and {victim} shouting this morning. {suspect} yelled: 'Over my dead body. Or yours!'
{victim} ordered {suspect} to be locked up on the village square tomorrow, for the whole village to throw rotten eggs at.
{victim} cut {suspect}'s wages in half this morning.
{victim} banned {suspect} from the library for good this morning, in front of everyone.
{victim} beat {suspect} at swordplay this morning, in front of the whole court, and laughed.
{suspect} asked {victim} to marry them this morning. {victim} laughed out loud.
{victim} served {suspect} spoiled fish this morning, as revenge for a complaint. {suspect} was ill all morning.
{victim} arrested {suspect}'s nephew in the village this morning. The boy might be banished from the kingdom.
{suspect} saw {victim} tearing pages out of the oldest book in the library this morning.
{victim} poured {suspect}'s finest bottle of wine out of the window this morning.
{victim} read {suspect}'s private letters this morning. Now they know everything.
{victim} told the King this morning that {suspect} cheated at the sword tournament.
{victim} caught {suspect} sneaking out of the castle last night. He's telling the King tomorrow.
{victim} put salt in {suspect}'s tea this morning, in front of everyone. The whole court laughed.
{victim} told the court this morning that {suspect} only pretended to be ill to skip their duties.
{victim} fined {suspect} a month's wages this morning. {suspect} dropped the oldest book in the library and it fell apart.
{victim} read {suspect}'s letter from home out loud in the staff room this morning.
{victim} told the King this morning that {suspect} writes secret letters to her homeland.
{victim} read {suspect}'s diary out loud at breakfast this morning.
{victim} spilled wine over {suspect}'s rarest book this morning, and just laughed.
{victim} called {suspect} a stupid brute who can't even read, in front of the whole court.
{victim} blamed {suspect} for the broken window this morning. Now {suspect} has to pay for it.

I'm off to the village market tonight for fresh ingredients. Don't expect me back before ten.
Note on the kitchen door: "Gone to the market for ingredients. Back late. – Chef"
{character} is sick in bed in the infirmary. Nobody is to disturb them today.
{character} lies sick in one of the infirmary beds.
{partner} and I have fencing lessons in the weaponry tonight, until late.
Leave me alone, this big cake must be done by midnight!
Note on kitchen door: "Busy with the big cake until midnight. Keep out!"
A letter on the desk: {character} travels to the neighbouring kingdom tonight for a state visit.
The lessons with {character} last until eight tonight.
Lesson schedule: {character}, lessons with {tutor} until eight tonight.
Tonight I have to visit a patient in the village. I won't be back before ten.
I'll be caring for {sick_character} all evening. I can't leave their side.
I can't leave, this medicine has to boil until eight.
Duty roster: night watch at the entrance tonight, the Head Guard.
I have the night watch at the entrance tonight.
I'm sharpening every weapon in the castle. I'll be busy until late tonight.
I have a terrible headache. I'm going to bed early tonight.
Note on the bedroom door: "Do not disturb, {character} is sleeping."
Staff board in the kitchen: "{character} – evening off"
I'm examining {character} tonight. Royal health comes first.
{character} asked me to keep the library open and the lamps lit until eight.
{character} is helping me with the preparations until eight.
I'll be doing the royal accounts in the study all evening.
I'll be counting every spoon of the silver tonight. Someone has been stealing.
I'm rehearsing my dance in the ballroom until eight. Everyone will be watching me.
Tonight I dine with my old war comrades! We'll be at it until late.
I have letters to write to my homeland tonight. I'll be in the study until nine.
A merchant in the village wants to see my work tonight. Good money.
A crate of new books arrived from the capital. I'll be cataloguing them in the library until nine.
Tonight I teach the kitchen staff their letters, from six until eight.
Guests arrive tomorrow. I'll be preparing the guest rooms until nine.
Drill and inspection for the whole guard tonight, from five until half past seven. No exceptions.
Tonight I bring bread to the families in the lower town. I'll be back late.
The ladies of the court are coming for tea in the pavilion tonight. I'll hear all the news first.
The young guards want to hear about my battles tonight! Can't disappoint them.
I shall be selecting the wines for tomorrow's banquet. It requires a refined palate and absolute silence.
I'm restoring the old castle maps in the study tonight. Delicate work, until eight.
Tonight the Doctor and I count every bottle in the infirmary.
The King wants his old armour polished for the ball. I'll be in the weaponry until eight.
Tonight I dissect a truly remarkable toad. It cannot wait a minute longer.
Some lords invited me to a game of cards in the pavilion tonight.
The ambassador's wife joins me for supper in the pavilion tonight. Diplomacy never sleeps.
Tonight I escort the treasurer's carriage to the village. I trust no one else with it.
Three new maids come to be interviewed tonight. I'll be in the staff room until eight.
The dressmaker comes at six with my gowns for the ball. I'll be trying them on until eight.
Tonight the King tastes my banquet menu. Seven courses, each one a masterpiece.
The village has begged me to judge their cooking contest tonight. Someone must show them what taste is.
The lords of the council want my report on the castle's defences tonight. I'll be in the study until eight.
Tonight I hear the troubles of the townsfolk in the village hall. Someone has to listen to them.
I'm giving a talk on the history of the castle at the village school tonight.
A colleague from the capital is visiting. We'll be talking medicine in the guest room until nine.
The Queen and I go over the household budget tonight, in the study.
My singing master comes at six. I'll be in the pavilion until eight, and everyone will hear me.
My old general rides in tonight! We'll be talking battles in the throne room until late.
Tonight the Head Guard and I go through the whole armoury, rack by rack.
My sister in the village had a baby today. I'm going to see her tonight.
I have a stack of letters to answer tonight. I'll be in the study until eight.
I'm practising with the crossbow in the weaponry tonight, until half past seven.
It's the innkeeper's birthday today. I'll be at the tavern in the village tonight.
{partner} has challenged me to chess in the pavilion tonight. It'll take hours.
It's a saint's day today. I'm going to evening mass in the village church.
{partner} has summoned me to the study tonight. We have much to discuss.
I'm riding out to the lake tonight. I need some air.
The miller's wife is having her baby tonight. I'll be in the village until it's born.
I'll be in the library tonight, reading up on a rare fever.
Mother and I are embroidering the banner for the ball tonight, in the pavilion.
{suspect} told me they'd be at {murder_place}, not {alibi_place} tonight.
The front door is broken. Nobody can leave the castle today.
{alibi_place} is closed tonight for repairs.
A note in the handwriting of {suspect}: "{murder_time}, {murder_place}. Don't be late."
{suspect} told me they'll be in {other_place} tonight.
Tonight with {suspect}? We have nothing planned.
I saw {suspect} trying the door of {murder_place} twice this afternoon.
{suspect} asked me for a dark cloak for tonight.
{suspect} asked me for the spare key to {murder_place} today.
Nobody is on my list to leave through the gate tonight.
{suspect} asked me the quickest route from {murder_place} to the castle gates.
{suspect} told me to cancel everything they had planned for tonight.
{suspect} asked me to cover for them tonight. If anyone asks, I'm to say they were in {alibi_place}.
{suspect} asked me to take their place at {alibi_place} tonight.
Letter from the neighbouring kingdom: "Our king has fallen ill. Tonight's visit is called off."
The big cake already stands finished and decorated in the pantry.
Updated duty roster: "Night watch tonight cancelled."
The grindstone in the armoury is cracked in two. Nothing can be sharpened with it.
The medicine is already bottled and labelled "ready".
The doctor's patient in the village is my brother. I saw him at the market this morning, healthy as a horse.
{suspect} asked me for a big supper tonight. Strange, for someone with a headache.
A note on the silver chest: "Counted and correct, this morning."
Note on the ballroom door: "All rehearsals cancelled tonight."
Letter: "Your Majesty, we regret that we cannot come tonight."
The morning messenger took all of the Queen's letters to her homeland. She told me she has nothing left to write today.
The village cooks told me the foreign merchant left the village yesterday, but never paid for his dinners. Extraordinarily rude.
The crate of books from the capital didn't come today. The cart is stuck on the road.
Note on the guards room door: "Drill cancelled tonight. Guards: free evening."
No ladies of the court are coming today. Their carriages are all in the capital.
The young guards are on duty in the village all evening.
Note on the wine rack: "Wines for tomorrow's banquet: selected and ready."
The kitchen staff have the evening off. Not one of them will be in the castle tonight.
Every loaf of bread in this castle is set aside for tomorrow's banquet.
The old castle maps went to the capital this morning to be copied. They won't be back tonight.
Nobody counts my bottles tonight. I locked the stores this morning and I'm keeping the key.
The King's old armour went to the village armourer this morning, for repairs.
The ambassador's wife fell ill this morning. She's staying in bed at the inn.
The treasurer left for the village at dawn. He took his own guards.
The new maids all took positions in the capital. Not one of them is coming to the castle.
The dressmaker's cart lost a wheel. She won't be here before tomorrow.
The banquet tasting is off tonight. The King has a toothache.
The lords all left for the hunt this morning. Nobody's playing cards tonight.
The village market is closed today for the saint's day.
The weaponry room is being cleaned tonight. Nobody trains in there until tomorrow.
No staff have the evening off tonight. Every pair of hands is needed.
The royal account books went to the treasurer in the village this morning.
Tomorrow's guests have cancelled. I was told this morning to cook for nobody extra.
Not a single patient in my infirmary today. Dreadfully dull.
The Doctor lost his remarkable toad this morning. It hopped straight into the well, and nobody is going down there for a toad.
The village cooking contest was called off today. Half the cooks are ill.
The lords of the council left for the capital this morning.
The village hall is locked tonight. The mayor shut it after a brawl this morning.
The village school is closed today. Half the children have the pox.
The physician from the capital sent word this morning. He isn't coming today.
The household budget was settled this morning. I've already been told to cook cheaper tonight.
The singing master has lost his voice. He sent word he won't come today.
The general's party was turned back at the border this morning. They won't reach the castle tonight.
There's no armoury inspection today. It isn't in my book.
{suspect}'s sister came to sell eggs at the castle this morning. She's expecting a baby, but she's nowhere near due.
The ink in the study ran out this morning. Not a drop until the merchant comes tomorrow.
At five I'm taking every crossbow down for repairs. Nobody shoots tonight.
The village tavern is shut tonight. The innkeeper is ill in bed.
There's no mass in the village tonight. The priest left for the capital this morning.
{suspect}'s horse hurt its leg this morning. It's not leaving the stable today.
The miller's wife had her baby this morning. A healthy boy.
The Doctor returned all my medical books this morning. He said he's done with them.
The library lamps are out of oil. The Librarian is closing early tonight.
I saw {character} buying poison this morning.
I asked {character} to buy rat poison. The cellar is full of rats.
I just saw {character} walking around with a dagger.
The Weapons master gave {character} a dagger as a present today.
